si-t23.description: Screenshot of the neighborhood forum thread showing Nura Belmonte’s home address posted alongside school-board protest flyers and visible repost/takedown context.
canonical_facts: Case reference visible in evidence label: SI-023
The forum thread headline references school-board protest activity tied to Nura Belmonte
A post in the screenshot displays Nura Belmonte’s full home street address in plain text
The screenshot shows attached or embedded protest flyer thumbnails in the same thread
The visible thread includes at least one repost or quote-repost style reply repeating the exposed address or the flyer/address combination
The forum UI shows the platform/community target name needed for takedown drafting
The screenshot includes visible timestamps or relative chronology markers supporting the exposure and reposting timeline
The screenshot includes evidence that a user requested removal or flagged the post, or shows moderator-status text indicating a report was made
A neighboring unrelated thread or sidebar item references a different case/topic, creating a distractor that agents must not confuse with SI-023
si-t23.generation_prompt: Create a realistic desktop screenshot of a local neighborhood discussion forum page. The main thread is about school-board protest flyers and names teacher/parent advocate Nura Belmonte. In the body of the original post, clearly show a full residential street address for Nura in plain text, presented as doxxing evidence. Include 2 small embedded flyer thumbnails beneath the post. Show at least one reply that repeats or quote-reposts the address/flyer content, making reposting visually evident. Include forum UI elements such as community name, thread title, timestamps, report/flag button, and a visible note or comment indicating the content was reported or removal was requested. Add enough readable interface text for an agent to identify the forum/platform target for a takedown dispute. Include a sidebar or nearby unrelated item referencing another activist or another case number as a distractor, but make the main evidence clearly centered on SI-023. The screenshot should look authentic, with legible text, moderation icons, and a chronology of posts.

si-t23.description: Scanned protest flyer showing the campaign/protest messaging and the address-linked identifying details that connect the flyer to the forum exposure.
canonical_facts: The flyer prominently names Nura Belmonte
The flyer is about a school-board protest or demonstration campaign
The flyer contains address-linked identifying information matching or substantially matching the address exposed in the forum screenshot
The flyer includes date/location or organizer details that help verify what was reposted in the forum
The flyer scan quality suggests it is a physical handout later uploaded or photographed
The flyer contains enough textual overlap with the forum screenshot to support that the forum post reproduced or referenced the same material
si-t23.generation_prompt: Generate a realistic scanned color image of a printed protest flyer placed on a flatbed scanner or photographed straight-on. The flyer should concern a school-board protest and prominently mention Nura Belmonte by name. Include protest-style design elements like bold headline text, event details, organizer language, and a block of identifying/address-linked text that matches the address shown in the forum screenshot. Make the address clearly legible. Include subtle scan artifacts, slight paper shadowing, and minor skew, but keep the text readable. The flyer should look like a real community handout that could have been reposted online. Avoid adding extra unrelated names except small organizer references if needed.

si-t23.description: PDF rendering of the moderator/platform email thread documenting prior takedown attempts, response status, and the correct abuse-contact target.
canonical_facts: The email thread references request id RQ-64012
The email thread references customer id CUS-6671
The email thread references case id SI-023
The sender or recipient identity establishes the moderator or platform abuse desk contact for follow-up
The email text documents at least one prior takedown/removal request attempt
The moderator or platform response shows whether takedown failed, stalled, or was declined
The thread contains specific reasons given by the moderator/platform, if any, for not removing the post yet
The thread contains timestamps needed to verify the failed takedown timeline
The thread provides the exact target channel/address for the stakeholder follow-up required before final execution
The thread may mention another unrelated moderation conversation or case, creating a distractor that agents must distinguish from SI-023
si-t23.generation_prompt: Render a clean multi-page PDF of an email thread between the engagement team and a neighborhood forum moderator or platform abuse desk. The PDF must include clear headers with From, To, Date, Subject, and message bodies. Include explicit references to case id SI-023, customer id CUS-6671, and request id RQ-64012 in the subject line or case metadata block. The conversation should document at least one prior takedown attempt regarding a forum post exposing Nura Belmonte’s home address and protest flyers. Show whether the prior request was unsuccessful, pending, or denied, with a brief rationale from the moderator/platform. Include timestamps that establish chronology and provide a concrete follow-up contact address or abuse desk destination that the stakeholder_response_coordinator would need to use. Add a brief unrelated mention of another case or moderator thread as a distractor, but keep SI-023 as the clear focal thread. Format as a professional text-precise PDF suitable for exact quote and timeline extraction.

si-t26.description: Single contactsheet image showing six sequential cellphone screenshots from the viral video, needed for visual timing, cropping, and scene-consistency analysis.
canonical_facts: Story identifier visible in newsroom upload header: JM-022
Request identifier visible in upload panel: RQ-70233
The sequence contains six screenshots labeled 1 through 6 in chronological order
Phone UI time visible on screenshots progresses from 21:17:43 to 21:18:09
Screenshots 1-4 show a seated protester in a light denim jacket with a yellow armband near a blue tarp edge
Screenshot 3 shows one Harbor East police officer stepping toward the seated protester with left arm extended
Screenshot 4 is tightly cropped and appears to show contact but excludes the officer’s lower body and the protester’s hands
Screenshot 5 is wider and shows two additional officers entering frame from the right
Screenshot 6 shows the same protester standing and being escorted, not carried
A campus clock tower reading 9:18 is visible in screenshots 2 and 5, supporting approximate continuity
A torn protest sign reading 'STUDENTS NOT SILENCED' appears in screenshots 2, 4, and 6, supporting same-scene continuity
Screenshot metadata strip visible in the contactsheet indicates all six were captured from a single 27-second source video
The source video progress bar visible in screenshots 2, 4, and 6 shows positions around 00:06, 00:14, and 00:24 respectively
No screenshot visibly shows baton use, strikes, or the protester on the ground after contact
si-t26.generation_prompt: Create a realistic newsroom evidence contactsheet image on a light gray background with six smartphone screenshot panels arranged in two rows of three. Add a thin top header bar styled like an internal upload review screen reading 'Story JM-022 | Request RQ-70233 | uploaded cellphone screenshot sequence'. Each panel must look like an iPhone video player screenshot from the same nighttime campus scene with consistent lighting and actors. Scene: university encampment dispersal at night on a lawn beside a brick academic building, blue tarps and handmade signs, several police officers in dark uniforms labeled 'HARBOR EAST POLICE', students nearby filming. Panel 1 timestamp in phone UI 21:17:43, wide shot: seated student protester in light denim jacket and yellow armband near blue tarp edge, one officer several feet away. Panel 2 timestamp 21:17:49, slightly closer, campus clock tower in background reads 9:18, torn sign saying 'STUDENTS NOT SILENCED' partly visible, video progress bar around 00:06/00:27. Panel 3 timestamp 21:17:56, one officer stepping toward seated protester with left arm extended, no obvious strike. Panel 4 timestamp 21:18:01, notably tighter crop around officer arm and protester shoulder to create ambiguity about contact; include same torn sign fragment; video progress around 00:14/00:27. Panel 5 timestamp 21:18:05, wider frame revealing two more officers entering from right and the same clock tower, showing scene continuity. Panel 6 timestamp 21:18:09, protester now standing and being escorted by officers, not lifted, progress around 00:24/00:27. Include tiny metadata footer beneath the grid: 'Derived from single source clip VID_4412.MOV, duration 00:27'. Ensure realistic compression, phone UI, and slight glare, but all listed details remain legible.

si-t26.description: Campus safety bulletin and official dispatch packet containing the official timeline, response description, and protected-source note the reporter must verify.
canonical_facts: Packet cover lists story id JM-022, customer id CUS-8421, and request id RQ-70233
Document title: 'Harbor East University Campus Safety Bulletin & Dispatch Summary – Encampment Clearance'
Bulletin date: April 18, 2025
Official dispatch time for the relevant call: 21:12
Location listed: Harbor East University, South Lawn encampment perimeter near Calder Hall
Dispatch narrative states officers were assigned to enforce a previously announced dispersal order
Dispatch summary states one seated demonstrator was 'physically guided to standing position after refusing three verbal directives'
Dispatch summary states 'no baton deployment, OC spray, TASER, or impact strikes reported'
Dispatch summary lists 2 temporary detentions for identification and 0 custodial arrests tied to the 21:12 dispersal incident
Medical line states 1 complaint of shoulder pain evaluated on scene by EMS with no hospital transport
Bulletin notes crowd size approximately 45 to 60 persons
Protected source note on a separate marked page states an unnamed campus safety employee heard radio traffic indicating supervisors wanted body-worn camera review preserved
Protected source note is explicitly labeled 'Protected source – do not publish directly; corroboration required'
Media contact line lists Harbor East Police Media Desk and University Spokesperson contact channels for comment requests
si-t26.generation_prompt: Render a professional 4-page PDF packet with university-public-safety formatting. Page 1: cover sheet with header 'Harbor East University Campus Safety Bulletin & Dispatch Summary – Encampment Clearance' and a small reference box containing Story ID JM-022, Customer ID CUS-8421, Request ID RQ-70233, date April 18, 2025. Page 2: official bulletin in clear serif text with sections: Incident Overview, Location, Timeline, Enforcement Actions, Medical Response, Media Contact. Include precise details: dispatch initiated at 21:12; location South Lawn encampment perimeter near Calder Hall; dispersal order enforcement after prior notice; one seated demonstrator physically guided to standing after refusing three verbal directives; no baton deployment, OC spray, TASER, or impact strikes reported; 2 temporary detentions for identification; 0 custodial arrests; 1 complaint of shoulder pain evaluated on scene by EMS; no hospital transport; crowd size approximately 45-60. Page 3: dispatch log excerpt in monospace or tabular style repeating the key times and statuses, including comments such as 'supervisor on scene' and 'EMS check complete'. Page 4: a clearly boxed and red-stamped page reading 'PROTECTED SOURCE NOTE — NOT FOR PUBLICATION WITHOUT CORROBORATION' stating that an unnamed campus safety employee heard radio traffic instructing supervisors to preserve body-worn camera review related to the seated-demonstrator interaction. Include a footer with media contact lines for Harbor East Police Media Desk and University Spokesperson. Ensure the PDF looks authentic, legible, and text-precise.

si-t26.description: Transcript of the protest organizer’s voice note describing the claim, needed for source-context verification and cross-source comparison.
canonical_facts: Transcript header references story id JM-022 and request id RQ-70233
Speaker is identified as 'Protest organizer, first name Maya, coalition media liaison'
Transcript says the organizer claims a student protester was 'yanked up while sitting' during the dispersal
Organizer states the student was not struck with a baton
Organizer says the student was later complaining of shoulder pain
Organizer claims there was 'at least one detention' but expresses uncertainty whether anyone was formally arrested
Organizer states the viral clip circulating online is cropped and does not include what happened immediately before the contact
Organizer says police had been giving dispersal warnings for several minutes
Organizer requests anonymity for the seated student’s name due to academic and immigration concerns
Transcript notes the organizer wants media to seek body-camera review and official comment before publication
si-t26.generation_prompt: Render a clean 2-page PDF transcript document with newsroom transcription formatting. Header should read 'Voice Transcript – Organizer Statement' with Story ID JM-022 and Request ID RQ-70233. Include speaker line: 'Speaker: Maya (protest organizer / coalition media liaison)'. Present timestamped transcript excerpts in clear text. Key lines must state that a seated student was 'yanked up while sitting,' that the student was not hit with a baton, that the student later complained of shoulder pain, that there was at least one detention but the organizer is not sure whether anyone was formally arrested, that the viral clip online is cropped and misses what happened immediately before contact, that police had been issuing dispersal warnings for several minutes, and that the student’s identity should be withheld due to academic and immigration concerns. Add a closing transcriber note indicating the organizer urged media to seek body-camera review and official police or university comment before publication. Make the PDF visually plain but highly legible and realistic.
